newsitem.title: BELGIUM: ATHLETICS - EL GUERROUJ SETS SECOND RECORD IN 10 DAYS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS - EL GUERROUJ SETS SECOND RECORD IN 10 DAYS.

text.p: Moroccan Hicham el Guerrouj smashed his second world indoor record in 10 days on Wednesday, beating the mile mark of three minutes 48.45 seconds at the Flanders athletics meeting.

After breaking the 1,500 metres record by nearly three seconds in Stuttgart, Germany, El Guerrouj beat the 3:49.78 set by Ireland's Eamonn Coghlan on February 27, 1983, in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
El Guerrouj, 22, was already one second below world record pace after just 200 metres and ran solo for the last 550 metres.
"It was such a fast race," he said.
He said the first part of the race, when he was paced by Australian Peter Stubbs and German Ruediger Stenzel, had been "too fast".

El Guerrouj, the 1995 world indoor champion, said he would now return to Morocco and only run a 1,500 metres indoor race in Stockholm on February 20 before starting preparations for the world outdoor championships in Athens in August.
He added he felt tired and would not try to better the 1,500 mark again in Stockholm.
He said he would miss the world indoor championships in Paris in March to focus entirely on Athens in a bid to become the first Moroccan world 1,500 metres outdoor champion.

El Guerrouj, who squandered his chances of winning Olympic gold when he fell just before the bell on the last lap of the final in Atlanta last August, said he had lost some energy because of the traditional Muslem Ramadan period.
"But I didn't lose any weight though," he added.
Mozambique's Maria Mutola failed in her bid to break the nine-year-old 800 metres indoor mark by German Christine Wachtel of 1:56.40.

Belgian pacesetter Katrien Maenhout started off too fast before fading quickly and Mutola, who was already 1.7 seconds behind world record pace after 400 metres, finished more than two seconds outside Wachtel's world mark.
"It was a very fast lap, the second was too slow and everything went wrong thereafter," Mutola said.
Mutola, who is to run next in Stockholm, said she felt capable of breaking Wachtel's record and would try whenever she felt in shape.
World record holder Colin Jackson of Britain won the 60 metres hurdles in 7.54 seconds, well outside his world mark of 7.30.

Fellow Briton Jamie Baulch upset world indoor champion Darnell Hall of the United States, a member of the gold-winning 4x400 metres Olympic relay team, to win the 400 metres by nearly one second in 45.45 seconds.
World record holder Irina Privalova set a year's best of 7.02 seconds over 60 metres, edging Nigerian Christy Opara who was awarded the same time.
Cuban Ivan Pedroso recorded the second best performance of the indoor season with a leap of 8.40 metres.
Another indoor season's second best was set by Belgian Eric Wymeersch over 200 metres. The European indoor champion sped round the track in 20.66 seconds.
